newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Tajik warlord remains in Tursunzade, official says.
newsitem.headline: Tajik warlord remains in Tursunzade, official says.

text.p: The rebel commander of the Tajik government's elite armoured brigade has not quit the aluminium producing town of Tursunzade as promised, a senior government official said on Friday.
"He has not left Tursunzade," Zafar Saidov, spokesman for Tajik President Imomali Rakhmonov said of the commander, colonel Makhmud Khudoyberdyev.
"He has moved only some of his armour back to (the nearby town of) Shakhrinau," Saidov told Reuters in the Tajik capital Dushanbe.

Khudoyberdyev, who led an armed revolt against the government in February last year, moved troops and tanks into Tursunzade, 45 km (30 miles) west of Dushanbe, on Wednesday to disarm local strongman Kodir Abdulayev.
He said he would leave the town on Thursday.
The colonel's move has alarmed Rakhmonov's shaky administration, which said Khudoyberdyev acted without orders.
"His actions were illegal," said Saidov. "We hope he obeys orders and returns to barracks."
Saidov said negotiations between the commander and the government were continuing on Friday.
The government of the remote former Soviet republic, which borders Afghanistan and China, is currently trying to negotiate an end to a bitter four-year civil war with Islamist opposition guerrillas.
A ceasefire appears to be holding but Khudoyberdyev's actions and a spate of shootings and bombings in the capital last week have sparked fears for the country's fragile peace.
